To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identify and characterize six RBPs that regulate the expression of one of the major ligands for NKG2D, MICB.
we identified six RNA-binding proteins that bind and regulate MICB expression and that at least two out of six identified RBPs regulate the expression of a major NKG2D stress-induced ligand.
we have identified six RNA-binding proteins that bind and regulate MICB expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that lead to the expression of NKG2DLs.
the mechanisms of immune cell activation and how this is linked to the recognition of stress-induced molecules by immune cells.
the molecular mechanisms of stress recognition by the immune system, which is a key step in the activation of cytotoxic T-cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of the MICB ligand is regulated by a number of RBPs that bind to the MICB transcript and are recruited to the MICB gene locus during genotoxic stress.
we have identified six RNA-binding proteins that bind to the mRNA of MICB and thereby regulate the expression of this immune activating ligand.
the RNA-binding proteins identified by us regulate the expression of stress-induced NKG2D-ligands.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of the activating ligand MICb can be modulated by RBPs and this modulation can have a profound impact on immune responses.
the immune system is a highly dynamic system that needs to be tightly regulated.
the RNA-binding protein HuR regulates MICB expression by binding to its mRNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of the stress-induced ligand MICB is tightly controlled by RBPs.
the expression of the ligand for the activating receptor Nkg2D is regulated by RBPs.
the expression of the activating ligand MIC-B is regulated by a network of RBPs, which are differentially recruited to the mRNA in response to different stressors.
